title: Why Do Dogs Howl? What Howling Means, Common Triggers & How to Stop It
summary: Why do dogs howl at sirens, at night, or when left alone? Learn what dog howling means, common triggers, and how to help your dog howl less.

The sudden howl your dog makes while lying by your side on a random evening raises a lot of questions as a pet parent. Could they be communicating with another dog somewhere far away? Are they calling out for something, or is it just a reflex? Howling in dogs can happen at different times and can mean different things. This article covers everything you need to know about howling in dogs: why dogs make sudden howls, what triggers them, and how to stop it.


**Content:**


1. Why Do Dogs Howl? What Howling Means
2. Common Triggers: Sirens, Music, the Moon & Other Dogs
3. Dogs Howling at Night and in Their Sleep
4. Howling When Left Alone & How to Help Your Dog Stop
5. Conclusion


## Why Do Dogs Howl? What Howling Means


[Barking](https://petcube.com/blog/dogs-dont-bark/) ,[whining](https://petcube.com/blog/dog-whining/) , and[growling](https://petcube.com/blog/my-dog-growl-when-i-pet-them/) aren’t the only sounds dogs make; they howl too. If you have ever caught your dog making a long, loud, and often melodious sound with their muzzle pointed up and neck stretched out, that might be howling. Don’t fret, your dog isn’t in danger. They might just be bored, lonely, or reacting to a sound they hear.


A[study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0168159199000118?ref=petcube.com) shows that dogs often howl due to[separation anxiety](https://petcube.com/blog/dog-separation-anxiety/) when they’re left home alone. Dogs can also howl for simple reasons, such as[marking territory](https://petcube.com/blog/stop-dog-from-marking/) , calling out to other dogs, or just showing emotions.


> “In some cases, dogs howl to express discomfort or pain, signaling something is wrong.”
> —[Reddit User](https://www.reddit.com/r/halocollarofficial/comments/1rscu7d/why_is_my_dog_howling_and_what_does_it_usually/?ref=petcube.com)


## Common Triggers: Sirens, Music, the Moon & Other Dogs


Dogs can howl in response to several triggers, such as sirens, music playing in the background, and even the moon. This behavior has been likened to that of wolves, and scientists are trying to find a link to howling in wolves. Some[research](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-023-04450-9?ref=petcube.com) has revealed that some dog breeds even reply to wolves’ howls, linking it to their genetic distance from wolves.


Dogs don’t howl without a trigger, just as they don’t bark for no reason. It’s always a response to something, whether a sound, an object, or movement. That said, they also howl to express emotions such as[fear](https://petcube.com/blog/dogs-panic-attacks/) and excitement. For example, a dog may howl at their pet parent after being apart for a while, which shows excitement and a wish to communicate.


## Dogs Howling at Night and in Their Sleep


Dogs may sometimes howl[at night](https://petcube.com/blog/dog-insomnia/) in reaction to faraway sounds that humans can’t easily hear. Dogs that patrol their surroundings at night may also howl when they notice subtle movement.


[Boredom](https://petcube.com/blog/is-my-dog-bored/) can also be a reason why dogs howl at night. The stillness and quiet of the night and the brightness of the moon can trigger a dog to howl.


Though uncommon, some dogs[howl while asleep](https://petcube.com/blog/dogs-howl-in-sleep/) . It can be unsettling for pet parents to see their dogs whine and howl in their sleep. This could be due to a[vivid dream](https://petcube.com/blog/what-do-dog-dream-about/) or, in rare cases, a neurological condition. It is important not to startle them when you notice this. Instead, record a video and show it to a veterinarian for a proper examination and diagnosis.


I had a dog who often howled while asleep. At first, I thought it was just due to vivid dreams. When it became more frequent, I took him for a check-up and found out he had a sleep behavior disorder. Sometimes, howling can be an early symptom of a neurological condition.


> “If your dog howls more than usual, it is necessary to take it to a vet to rule out any form of illness or injury.”
> —[Dr. Zubair Khalid](https://www.zubairkhalid.com/knowledge/veterinary-medicine/behavior/dog-howl-causes-and-stopping?ref=petcube.com)


## Howling When Left Alone & How to Help Your Dog Stop


Many pet parents[leave their dogs home alone](https://petcube.com/blog/bad-dog-owner/) when they go out, and this can make a dog feel very lonely and bored. Out of loneliness and boredom, dogs left at home may howl and whine. Pet parents can keep an eye on their dog with a[Petcube Cam](https://petcube.com/cam/?ref=petcube.com) paired with the[Petcube App](https://petcube.com/mobile-app/?ref=petcube.com) , and use the two-way audio feature to talk to them. Hearing your voice can help your dog feel relaxed, safe, and close to you.


## Conclusion


Dog howling shouldn’t feel strange; it’s a natural and normal response in dogs. Dogs howl for different reasons, which can be as simple as greeting their pet parent, reacting to sounds, feeling lonely or bored, or calling out to other dogs. So the next time your dog howls in the dark or at the moon, don’t fret. They might just be reaching out to a dog friend or doing what dogs do best: howling at the moon.
